stories.title: U.S. grounds flights days after Trump administration expands new AI air traffic system
stories.simple_summary: The U.S. government stopped all airplane flights for a few days after starting to use a new AI system to manage air traffic. Officials are now investigating whether the AI system caused the problem.
stories.why_it_matters: If you fly or depend on people flying goods to you, this matters. We need to make sure new technology is tested carefully before it affects something as important as flying.

stories.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is building a giant catalog of information about every product sold anywhere on the internet, including products it doesn't sell itself. It wants to show all this information on Amazon's website.
stories.why_it_matters: If you sell products online or run a small store, Amazon may now make it harder for customers to leave and shop elsewhere, since everything they need is in one place.

stories.title: FAA investigating whether new AI technology contributed to nationwide ground stop
stories.simple_summary: The government's aviation safety agency is looking into whether the new AI air traffic system played a role in the nationwide ground stop that happened recently.
stories.why_it_matters: This is part of the same flight shutdown story. It shows that safety officials are being careful about investigating what went wrong.

stories.title: Entire US Airspace Shut Down Days After the FAA Rolled Out an AI Air Traffic Tool. Was It a Coincidence?
stories.simple_summary: Days after the government rolled out a new AI tool to manage air traffic, all U.S. flights were grounded. People are wondering if the AI tool caused it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is the same major story as the other flight headlines. The takeaway is that when new technology runs important systems, problems can affect millions of people quickly.

stories.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
stories.simple_summary: Jensen Huang is stepping down from leading Nvidia, a major company that makes computer chips for AI. Other companies that wanted his money and support for AI startups are now worried he won't give them as much.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and startup founders. There's nothing you need to do, but it shows changes happening at the top of the AI industry.

stories.title: AI risks are the biggest threat to the financial system, Fed survey finds
stories.simple_summary: The Federal Reserve, which oversees U.S. banks, surveyed financial experts and found they think AI poses the biggest risk to the banking system right now.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have a bank account or savings, this matters. Banks need to make sure AI systems don't cause new types of problems or fraud.

stories.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is now letting its AI assistants use a digital wallet to buy things on your behalf. You can link your credit card, and the AI can make purchases without you typing in the order.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT, you should understand that this feature lets AI spend your money automatically. Be careful about which AI agents you give wallet access to.

stories.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
stories.simple_summary: LangChain, a company that helps other companies build and run AI systems, was just valued at 3 billion dollars. This is a significant valuation jump.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies. It shows that businesses are spending money to build better AI tools.

stories.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
stories.simple_summary: Research shows that China's most advanced AI systems were trained using expensive computer chips that the U.S. government banned from selling to China. This means China found a way around the restrictions.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters because it involves national security between the U.S. and China. It's a complex political situation with no immediate effect on ordinary people or small businesses.

stories.title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is testing a feature that lets AI agents use a digital wallet to shop online for you. You put in your credit card information, and the AI can complete purchases.
stories.why_it_matters: This is similar to the other ChatGPT Wallet story. Only early users can test it now, but understand that giving AI control over your wallet means it can spend money.

stories.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
stories.simple_summary: Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, has resigned from his job following personal issues. This could affect national security because Nvidia is central to the competition between the U.S. and China for advanced AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a business and politics story. There's nothing you need to do personally, but leadership changes at major tech companies can ripple through the industry.

stories.title: What’s really at stake in the Jensen Huang saga
stories.simple_summary: With Jensen Huang stepping down from Nvidia, people are now examining bigger questions about Nvidia's business dealings with China and whether the U.S. government will investigate or change its policies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly affects investors and government policy makers. It shows that Nvidia's leadership change has opened up larger questions about how AI companies do business internationally.
